title: The Underrated Art of Sound: Exploring the Impact of Sound Mixing in Movies

commenti.body:
Imagine Star Wars without:

The sound of light sabers
The roar of the TIE fighters
Darth Vader's breathing
R2FD2

Off the top of my head, some films I think of with memorable sound are:

The Exorcist, for jarring sound cuts
Blow Out. John Travolta plays a sound engineer who discovers a conspiracy in a role that inspired QT to cast him in Pulp Fiction
Blade Runner
Alien
Aliens (the tracker, the sound of the pulse rifles)
Arrival
Roma (not for flash, just pure emotional immersion)
No Country For Old Men
Annihilation 
Apocalypse Now
Trainspotting (for the incredible music placement) 
Baby Driver (opening sequencel

That's an amazing list. I find sound design to be a universal language; whether it's a foreign film or from a different culture, the nuances in sound cues and scores consistently guide me in grasping the scene's tone and comprehension effortlessly.

The sound in Robert Eggers The Witch added so much to the film. I had a few jump scares in this movie from the sound alone let alone the visuals. His use of sound in The Lighthouse is memorable but it was The Witch will always make me think sound first over anything else.

A lot of people were praising the sound on Fincher’s new movie The Killer. What in particular did people love about the sound. Was it sound editing? Fincher’s attention to detail?

I tutor on a sound design masters course and we start the students off every year with "Sound of Metal" and end with "Under the Skin".

As Steven Benedict said on his podcast, "Calling film a visual medium is a cliché which hasn't been true since 1927" (the year of the sound film).

I'm currently developing a podcast to focus on sound design and sound editing in films with a friend of mine. I'd love to hear what people think we should focus on! We haven't started uploading our episodes yet, but our first episode involves analyzing (using software) a very complex sound in a sci-fi film and then recreating it ourselves with foley and processing. And the second episode is a much more casual reaction to a new film with interesting sound design.

**My number 1: Blade Runner 2049**
The way it seemlessly blends the Hans Zimmer and Benjamin Wallfisch score with the sound effects is so good.

**Number 2: The Tree of Life**
Not only is the Lacrimosa soundtrack, created by the legend Zbigniew Preisner, greatly used to enhance the visuals, it is also a beautiful musical piece. The sound effects in this film are also very soft and peaceful, contributing to the dreamlike atmosphere of the film.

**Number 3: Harry Potter**
How magical would Harry Potter be without John Williams? Even if the last 5 films were composed by other composers, they were still inspired by Williams.

**Number 4: The Double Life of Veronique**
I don't think the sound effects are necessarily good, but the soundtrack my Zbigniew Preisner (aka Van den Budenmayer) is one of the best musical pieces in existence.

**Number 5: Last and First Men**
Directed and composed by Jóhann Jóhannsson. When both the cinematography and score are directed by a singular mind, it can result in complete harmony between the two.
That's very interesting. Once you upload, Please can you leave a link down here on this thread? Thanks in advance

Ryusuke Hamaguchi's "Asako I & II" might not come off as a movie that relies on sound design but, it actually is. A couple scenes really made me appreciate what sound can do in terms of storytelling for the first time.

On the other hand, lack of sound can be used skillfully too. A Korean series called 'Stranger' has a scene where the protagonist is searching for clues in the house of a kidnapped character. It has no sound but, it was so haunting.

Come and see. You know, the classic scene of the kids arriving to their little town to find something has gone terribly wrong and the only thing that you keep hearing is a fly buzzing in your ear, which causes all sorts of tension. There are all sorts of techniques that the movie employs to deepen the story and to make it more disturbing than it already is. That movie is horrifying even though visually there is not much horrific material, because the sound design helps build an atmosphere of pure terror which sticks with you forever after you watch it. For me at least, if you have seen it, I'd like to know your comments.
Thanks for your recommendations, It really looks interesting. I really like War related movies as they specifically need great sound mixing for world building. I will get back to you once I watch it.
